newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease on profit-taking, trade calmer.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease on profit-taking, trade calmer.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased in calm trading on profit-taking after a two-day rise on news of Russia's new Eurobond and the unfreezing of some MinFins, dealers said on Friday.
Joint lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg said on Thursday a $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond would be priced to yield 345 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

Mikhail Ignatyev, a detective in the investigations department of the fifth central Moscow police precinct, told Reuters on Thursday he had issued an order to unfreeze $56.81 million of MinFin bonds which he had frozen in June in connection with an investigation into the theft of securities.
"The day has been calm compared to the previous two days. The market has got overheated and today prices eased apparently on profit-taking," one dealer said.
Dealers said trading could also be calmer because banks were trading for the second day with the same one-week settlement date, November 29, which is Thanksgiving Day holiday in the U.S.
MinFin bond operators use U.S. banks for settlements.
